items.stem: A small spherical ball of radius r falls through a viscous liquid with terminal velocity v. If another sphere of same material but radius 2r falls through the same liquid, its terminal velocity will be:
items.shortSolution: Terminal velocity is proportional to the square of the radius (r^2). Thus, doubling the radius quadruples the terminal velocity.

items.stem: A coil of 100 turns and area 0.1 m^2 is placed perpendicular to a magnetic field. If the magnetic field changes uniformly from 0.2 T to 0.6 T in 0.2 seconds, calculate the magnitude of induced emf in volts.
items.shortSolution: Induced emf = N * (delta B * A) / delta t = 100 * ((0.6 - 0.2) * 0.1) / 0.2 = 20 V.

items.stem: For a rigid diatomic gas molecule, what is the molar heat capacity at constant volume (Cv) in terms of the gas constant R?
items.shortSolution: A rigid diatomic molecule has 5 degrees of freedom (3 translational and 2 rotational). Hence, Cv = (f/2)R = (5/2)R.

items.stem: A body of mass 0.5 kg executes SHM attached to a spring of force constant k = 200 N/m. Find its angular frequency in rad/s.
items.shortSolution: Angular frequency omega = sqrt(k/m) = sqrt(200 / 0.5) = sqrt(400) = 20 rad/s.

items.stem: According to Huygens principle, light waves propagate through space by forming:
items.answer: Secondary wavelets from every point on a wavefront
items.shortSolution: Huygens principle states that every point on a primary wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical wavelets.
options: Secondary wavelets from every point on a wavefront

items.stem: A stretched string of length L fixed at both ends oscillates in its fundamental mode. The wavelength of the standing wave formed is:
items.shortSolution: In fundamental mode, length L = wavelength / 2, which gives wavelength = 2L.

items.stem: Two long parallel straight wires separated by a distance of 0.2 m carry currents of 5 A and 10 A in the same direction. Calculate the force per unit length between them in micro-Newton per meter.
Two particles of masses 2 kg and 3 kg are located at x = 1 m and x = 6 m respectively along a straight line. Find the x-coordinate of the center of mass in meters.
When determining the refractive index of a glass slab using a travelling microscope, the apparent shift depends directly on:
items.answer: Real thickness of the slab and its refractive index
items.shortSolution: Apparent shift = t * (1 - 1/mu), which depends on both real thickness t and refractive index mu.
options: Real thickness of the slab and its refractive index
Only the surface area of the glass slab
Only the magnification of the microscope

items.stem: Which of the following amines exhibits the highest basic strength in aqueous solution?
items.shortSolution: In aqueous solution, secondary methylamine (CH3)2NH is the strongest base due to a balance of inductive effect, solvation, and steric hindrance.

items.stem: Which of the following carbocations is expected to be the most stable?
items.shortSolution: Tert-butyl carbocation (CH3)3C+ has 9 hyperconjugative alpha-hydrogens and high inductive stabilization, making it the most stable among the options.

items.stem: A chemical reaction has delta H = -40 kJ and delta S = -100 J/K. Determine the maximum temperature in Kelvin up to which this reaction remains spontaneous.
items.shortSolution: For spontaneity, delta G = delta H - T*delta S < 0. Setting delta G = 0 gives T = delta H / delta S = -40000 / -100 = 400 K.
